name: Archaeological Zone of Paquimé, Casas Grandes
description: Paquimé is a ruined adobe town in northern Chihuahua, Mexico, set in a broad river valley about 240 km northwest of the state capital. Settled after 1130 and rebuilt into multi-storied dwellings after 1350, it linked the Pueblo peoples of the American Southwest with Mesoamerica. Irrigation fed its farmland, and the earthen walls you can walk among today are only part of the original city, which was abandoned around 1450.
